subject: programming-and-data-structures

chosen.title: Data structures: Binary Search Tree
covers: the cost comparison against arrays and linked lists
the search-tree rule
search, insertion and deletion costs
the balanced average case and the skewed worst case
chosen.why: The clearest beginner explanation of why a search tree exists at all, and the only lecture whose text was readable here. Read in part: the page extraction returned the lecture from its opening through the definition, the search and the insertion and deletion costs, and stopped inside the discussion of large inputs, so the later balancing remarks are not used and no card quotes it.

chosen.channel: NPTEL / Chennai Mathematical Institute, Madhavan Mukund
chosen.title: Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, Week 7 Lecture 4: Dynamic sorted data and binary search trees
covers: the search-tree rule with no duplicates
inorder as a sort
find, minimum and maximum
insertion at a leaf
the three deletion cases with the left-subtree maximum as replacement
complexity equal to the height, O(log n) when balanced
chosen.why: An official NPTEL course handout, readable in full, that states every search-tree operation together with the deletion cases and the height-bounded complexity. It is the only candidate whose complete text could be read, and it supplies the deletion rule that the GATE questions depend on.

chosen.title: Binary tree
covers: at most two children
full, complete and perfect definitions
the array representation of a complete tree
chosen.why: The correctness anchor for the shape vocabulary, because GATE questions turn on the difference between full, complete and perfect. Read in part: the extraction returned the definitions section.

chosen.title: Tree traversal
covers: the three depth-first orders
stack for depth first and queue for breadth first
inorder on a search tree giving ascending keys
the statement that a pair including inorder fixes the tree and preorder with postorder does not
chosen.why: The only readable source found that states the uniqueness result for traversal pairs in the same place as the three orders, which is what the 2004 question tests. Read in part: the extraction returned the types and depth-first sections.

chosen.title: Binary expression tree
covers: the stack construction from a postfix string
the worked example a b + c d e + * *
chosen.why: Used for the one applications card, because it gives the construction and a worked example that can be recomputed. It is a single source for that card, which is why the card is P3 and the topic stays partial.

chosen.title: Previous GATE questions in Data Structures
covers: the list of GATE questions from 2025 and 2026 that fall in this topic
chosen.why: Used to fix the scope of the topic against the actual paper record: it shows which tree and search-tree questions the recent papers asked, which is how the subtopic enumeration was checked. Read in part: the extraction returned the index with question openings.

chosen.title: Question pages for GATE CSE 2004 Q.35, 2016 Set 2 Q.40, 2017 Set 1 Q.6, 2017 Set 2 Q.36, 2020 Q.5, 2024 Set 2 Q.29, 2025 Set 1 Q.16, 2025 Set 2 Q.3, 2025 Set 2 Q.25 and 2026 Set 1 Q.52
covers: the ten question statements, options and accepted answers
chosen.why: Each PYQ record cites its own page. Read in part: statement, options and the accepted answers were read; no official key document was fetched, so every record is labelled SOURCED rather than OFFICIAL_KEY.
